purpose: Curated forward-testable source material for translating web-development knowledge into AstylarUI.

sourceContract.fixtureBacked: fixtureSource contains reference.html, reference.css, and the equivalent siteData.root/siteData.styles; the parity harness executes both forms in the same Chromium environment.
sourceContract.inline: web contains reference HTML/CSS and astylar.siteData contains the equivalent serializable document. hostCode records required Angular/Astylar lifecycle behavior outside SiteData.
sourceContract.verification: npm run examples:check validates this manifest; npm run parity:check executes the fixture-backed visual/behavioral pairs.

examples.title: Semantic landmarks, text, links, lists, and tables
directMappings: HTML tag names map to DOMElement.type aliases.
id, text, children, href, scope, and authored order retain their ordinary meanings.
CSS declarations become camelCase fields on SiteData.styles rules.
importantDifferences: SiteData is serializable authored data, not a live browser Node tree.
Astylar paints Babylon meshes and mirrors the supported semantics through an offscreen accessibility bridge.

examples.title: Block flow and the CSS box model
directMappings: width, height, padding, margin, border, background, and normal block flow use familiar CSS concepts.
The same authored IDs identify both browser boxes and Astylar meshes for parity measurement.
importantDifferences: The visual box is Babylon geometry projected to the canvas; measured CSS pixels are converted to scene units internally.

examples.title: Responsive viewport rules
directMappings: Viewport units, source order, breakpoint intent, and responsive sizing transfer directly.
Surface resize recomputes the same document against the new canvas viewport.
importantDifferences: Instead of CSS @media blocks, each JSON rule carries mediaMinWidth/mediaMaxWidth/mediaMinHeight/mediaMaxHeight bounds.
The host calls surface.resize() or relies on AstylarSurfaceComponent resize observation.

examples.title: Inherited typography and measured text
directMappings: Font family, size, weight, style, color, line height, spacing, alignment, and inherited values use CSS-like declarations.
Nested text receives inherited values through the Astylar cascade.
importantDifferences: Text is measured and painted through canvas/Babylon resources, so available fonts and browser canvas metrics define the fidelity boundary.
Astylar implements a focused typography subset rather than every CSS text property.

examples.title: Interactive form controls and validation
directMappings: Form, label, input and button structure; required/pattern constraints; focus; keyboard editing; and submit intent follow the tested browser model.
Typed event names and authored IDs remain familiar.
importantDifferences: Executable onclick strings are not evaluated; handlers live in AstylarRenderOptions.events.
Control behavior is a documented subset and state is reconciled across surface.update() rather than mutated through DOM APIs.

examples.title: Positioning, stacking, and modal focus containment
directMappings: dialog identity, open state, fixed positioning, z-index intent, autofocus, Escape cancel, and wrapped Tab navigation transfer to the supported subset.
importantDifferences: DOMElement.modal is the explicit Astylar opt-in corresponding to showModal() behavior.
Astylar does not synthesize browser ::backdrop paint; author a backdrop element/style when it is visually required.

examples.title: Asynchronously ready image assets
directMappings: img, src, alt, intrinsic sizing, explicit dimensions, and object-fit use familiar authoring concepts.
surface.whenSettled() provides a deterministic host boundary for asynchronously ready owned resources.
importantDifferences: Image textures are Babylon resources owned by the surface/generation rather than browser image elements.
Use deterministic local or data assets for SSR, tests, and offline consumers.

examples.title: Ordinary generated Tailwind utilities loaded from Angular global CSS
directMappings: Generated Tailwind CSS remains an ordinary Angular global stylesheet and DOMElement.class uses normal static class strings.
Supported utility results for layout, spacing, typography, paint, responsive variants, states, controls, and overflow enter the existing typed renderer pipeline.
importantDifferences: Applications enable document stylesheet discovery once with provideAstylar({ css: { useDocumentStyles: true } }); no compiler call or stylesheet registration is added to SiteData.

Only inspectable applicable CSS and supported final Astylar properties transfer. Tailwind must be able to discover complete static class names; dynamically assembled partial class names are outside this proof.
Loaded styles sit below SiteData.styles and DOMElement.style in the Astylar cascade, so typed rules remain deliberate overrides.

examples.title: A web-authored card inside an owned Babylon scene

web.css: #card { width: 280px; padding: 20px; background: #172554; color: white; border-radius: 12px; } #card h2, #card p { margin: 0; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; } #card p { margin-top: 10px; }

astylar.hostCode: const surface = astylar.mount(canvas, siteData, { clearColor: new Color4(0.01, 0.02, 0.08, 1), setupLighting: scene => setupHostLighting(scene) }); await surface.whenSettled(); // The host may inspect surface.scene, but must dispose surface ownership as a unit.

directMappings: The semantic card tree, CSS-like sizing, spacing, type, color, and radius remain ordinary Astylar document data.
importantDifferences: The host owns a canvas, camera-facing Babylon scene, lighting callback, and disposable AstylarSurface rather than a browser document viewport.
CSS-like pixels are converted into scene geometry; direct Babylon customization belongs in host setup or a plugin, not arbitrary SiteData fields.

examples.title: Replace CSS transitions with explicit application state

web.css: #save { background: #2563eb; transition: background 180ms ease, transform 180ms ease; } #save:hover { background: #1d4ed8; transform: translateY(-2px); }

astylar.hostCode: Use immediate supported :hover/:active paint for interaction feedback. For meaningful state changes, update an Angular signal and pass the resulting SiteData to surface.update(); for real 3D motion, use a lifecycle-owned plugin/Babylon animation.

directMappings: The button structure and the supported normal/hover background states transfer directly.
importantDifferences: Astylar does not parse transition, animation, or @keyframes, so it intentionally shows the supported hover state immediately.
Application state and plugin-owned Babylon animation are explicit alternatives; silently copying animation CSS would be incorrect.

examples.title: Angular plugin-backed custom element and style property

web.css: consumer-badge { display: block; width: 180px; height: 44px; background: #7c3aed; --badge-depth: 0.12; }

astylar.hostCode: Register provideConsumerBadgePlugin(...) in the Angular providers for each application configuration. The plugin validates data/extensions, injects surface state, owns Babylon resources, and requests safe invalidation.

directMappings: The custom component identity, dimensions, background, and authored payload intent remain declarative.
importantDifferences: Astylar custom elements/properties require a versioned persisted plugin requirement and a trusted Angular provider contribution; CSS custom properties do not register renderer behavior.
Plugin-owned async Babylon resources must use generation/surface ownership and DestroyRef rather than escaping the surface lifecycle.
